title: 10,000-GPU Fleet Gang-Scheduler with NVLink / InfiniBand RoCE Cross-Rack Topology
subtitle: Distributed Training Topology-Aware Gang-Scheduling, Straggler Mitigation and Checkpoint I/O
problem_statement: A frontier AI research lab trains 1-trillion parameter MoE models across 10,000 NVIDIA H100 GPUs. The cluster suffers 42% MFU (Model Flops Utilization) losses due to fragmented node scheduling (non-contiguous rack allocation), straggler GPUs with degraded PCIe links, and 45-minute checkpoint write stalls.

faded_bug.description: Greedy non-topology-aware allocation splits Ring-AllReduce ranks across oversubscribed spine switches, multiplying communication latency.

studio_1_runtime.correct_fix_diff:
+ // Implement Rail-Aligned, Non-Blocking Fat-Tree Switch Allocator
+ selected_nodes = self.allocate_rail_aligned_clique(job_gpu_count)

invariants.description: Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU) across the 10,000 GPU cluster must remain >= 60%.

probing_ladder.stage_1_validation: Explain the difference between Tensor Parallelism (TP), Pipeline Parallelism (PP), and Data Parallelism (DP/FSDP). Which require NVLink vs InfiniBand?
probing_ladder.stage_2_tightening: If a single GPU out of 10,000 suffers memory throttling and slows down by 15%, what happens to the entire training run under synchronous All-Reduce?
probing_ladder.stage_3_adversarial: Checkpointing 1 Terabyte of model weights every 30 minutes halts training. How does asynchronous asynchronous distributed checkpointing to NVMe over Fabrics (NVMe-oF) eliminate write stalls?
probing_ladder.stage_4_squeeze: A 10,000 GPU cluster consumes 12 Megawatts of power. How do you design an automated straggler detection and node eviction engine that saves $50,000 per hour of wasted training?

counter_probes.counter_question: Standard TCP Ethernet has packet drops, kernel buffer copies, and tail latency under incast congestion. Why does large-scale distributed training require RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE v2) or InfiniBand?
counter_probes.expected_staff_answer: TCP kernel overhead and buffer drops devastate Ring-AllReduce throughput. RoCE v2 with Priority Flow Control (PFC) and Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN) provides hardware zero-copy bypass and deterministic latency.
